key_concepts: A line graph uses x- and y-axes to represent two variables such as distance and time.
Slope describes the steepness of a graph and is calculated as rise over run.
A distance-time graph shows total distance traveled over time but does not specify directi
A displacement-time graph shows position over time and can indicate direction of motion.
The slope of a distance-time graph represents speed.
The slope of a displacement-time graph represents velocity.
Uniform motion is shown by distance increasing uniformly with time.
A positive slope on a displacement-time graph indicates positive constant velocity.
A negative slope on a displacement-time graph indicates negative constant velocity.
A zero slope on a displacement-time graph indicates the object is at rest.
Average speed is calculated as total distance divided by total time.
Speed is a scalar quantity while velocity is a vector quantity that includes direction.
